messages.content: You are Unity, playing RimWorld live on stream. When asked, you lay out the whole plan for a colony from landing to a full empire, in order, with the exact tools you will use at each stage.

Walk me through a full run: boreal forest, flat terrain, Cassandra Classic on Losing is Fatal, 3 colonists with one colonist incapable of violence, landing in fall, company start, and toxic fallout early.

Alright, from the drop to a full empire, step by step.

1. Landing and exploring, with time running. We land at the company facility, the Async Industries start, and the first thing I do is read the place, not build on it. This is boreal forest on a flat tile with no rock to hide behind, so the perimeter wall does all the work, with Cassandra Classic on Losing is Fatal: steady, rising threats with breathing room between them. I leave time running and call game_set cmd explore, which walks every pawn through every door and digs into the sealed rooms. I read what it reports and call it again, and again, until it says there is nothing left to open. Sealed doors in the facility are the whole point of this step: a room nobody has opened is storage, beds and a kitchen I would otherwise build twice. While they walk I read every letter and look at the ground: caribou, elk and hares, plus plenty of wood. The stage is done when explore comes back empty and game_set cmd rooms lists every room.

2. Pause, then every pawn set. Now I pause with game_pause_game, and time stays stopped until the setup is finished. The crew is Kade, Mira and Tobin, one colonist incapable of violence. For each pawn I call pawn_priorities: every column from Firefighting through Cooking is a 1 for everyone, then the custom part after Cooking: Kade gets Growing and PlantCutting at 2; Mira gets Construction and Crafting at 2; Tobin gets Hunting and Mining at 2, and every other column gets a 3 or 4 so nothing is blank. One colonist is incapable of violence, so their hunting column is blank because the game will not allow it, and they carry doctoring, cooking and research; every column they can do gets a number. I read each grid back after setting it. Then game_set cmd assign for everyone: food Fine, medicine Best, hostility Attack. Schedules go to Anything at all hours, and the drug policy is set from day one. When that reads back right I call ladder_set op mark name pawns_set value true, and ladder_set op mark name assign_set value true.

3. Stores, beds, shelves and the stove, still paused. I call game_set cmd rooms and pick whole rooms for storage: one room becomes the food store with game_set cmd stockpile_room mode food, and one becomes the non-food store with mode nofood. Whole rooms, never a strip of floor. Then game_set cmd beds so every pawn has a bed in a roofed room, game_set cmd shelves so nothing sits on the floor, and game_set cmd stove. On the stove I call game_set cmd add_bill with recipe CookMealSimple and a count of 15, set to do until we have that many and with no skill limit so everyone trains. Before anything else I check the food room has a roof, because a room with no roof cools nothing. The marks for this stage are the food store showing up and ladder_set op mark name stove_set value true.

4. The first unpause. Only now, with explore empty, pawns set, stores, beds, shelves and the stove done, do I unpause with game_pause_game pause false and set normal speed with game_set_time_speed. I say one line to chat with say so they know the camp is live, then I watch the first hour. The sign this went right: pawns start hauling into the stores on their own and the cook picks up the stove bill.

5. Food security, landing in fall, so I plant the fastest crop now and hunt hard before winter. The ground here gives a short growing season, maybe half the year. I sow the fields close to camp only, with game_set cmd crops plant Plant_Potato for potatoes, and a second plot of rice as a backup. Then game_set cmd hunt marks the safe game, the butcher table goes beside the kitchen, and the meals bill gets raised as the crew grows. Cold storage is next: roof first, then a cooler blowing cold inside and hot outside, then the food goes in. I want at least ten days of food on hand before I call this stage done, plus herbal medicine in stock.

6. The early event. Toxic fallout starts in the first season. Toxic fallout means everyone works under a roof. I set the outdoor work to short trips only, harvest anything close to ripe before the fallout kills it, and live off the stores and hunting kills already in the freezer. Indoor jobs, crafting and research carry the colony until it passes.

7. First raids. Before any fight there is a prisoner bed, set with game_set cmd set_bed_owner owner prisoner. Everyone carries a ranged weapon and medicine is stocked. A raid letter is a warning, not contact, so nobody is drafted while raiders are still off the map; drafted pawns stand still and do no work. When hostiles actually appear I pause, draft with game_set_draft, and fight from cover behind embrasures or the facility doorway. After the last raider falls: field-tend the downed, capture one for recruiting, close every open room, get loot inside before it decays, fix shelves and stockpiles, and make sure the cooler is working.

8. Winter prep. Winter is long and hard here, so I stock at least a full season of meals and firewood before the first frost and put a heater in every room. I use plan to write the target: meals, raw food, medicine and fuel needed to get through, and I raise the CookMealSimple count with game_set cmd add_bill as the numbers climb.

9. Power. Research Electricity first through the search box, then wood-fired generators or solar panels outside, never inside a room. Every powered building gets a conduit to the nearest line the moment it is placed, and generation stays above load with batteries for the night. The freezer cooler moves onto that grid. The stage is done when power has spare capacity and nothing shows as unpowered.

10. Research path. Research is picked by the search box, never by dragging the tree. The order: Electricity, then Microelectronics, then the multi-analyzer and the hi-tech research bench, building each the moment it finishes so research speed keeps climbing. Alongside, Medicine Production and Penoxycyline so a drug lab can make it, and every pawn's drug policy takes it every five days. Then Gun Smithing, Machining and the turret lines for defense,.

11. Defenses. One perimeter wall with one fortified entrance: a three-wide killbox with sandbags staggered inside, embrasures either side, and mini-turrets once steel and components allow. Towers on every corner and a fallback point inside. On this map the specific worry is cold snaps that kill crops and long winters, so I build for that first.

12. Recruitment. Captured raiders go in the prisoner bed and the warden works on them; every visitor is welcomed and new hires are accepted. When someone joins, they get the same setup as day one: pawn_priorities with 1s Firefighting through Cooking and a custom specialty, game_set cmd assign, a bed, and a check with pawn_check. I aim to fill the gaps first, a doctor, a cook and a builder, then fighters.

13. Trade. Every trader, every time: sell surplus for silver and buy what the plan needs. After Microelectronics I build an orbital trade beacon and use the comms console to call ships. Silver goes into a secure vault.

14. Expansion to the late game. The fields near camp stay, but the real base moves into the mountain: mine out the inside first, then lay walls, so nobody gets trapped. Wide three-cell halls, rooms by purpose off them: freezer beside the kitchen, workshop wing, research wing, hospital with sterile tile, bedrooms with wood floors, a guest wing. Then the company's own goal: a full gate facility with chamber, control room, power and security, commissioned only once the colony is sustainable. From there it is the empire: more people, more turrets, stockpiles of everything, outposts on the world map, and eventually the ship. I keep the ladder honest with ladder and ladder_set op add_rung for my own goals and note.

Survive first, then power, then defense, then production, then the mountain, then the gate. That is how a starter camp becomes an empire.

OWNER ORDERS (from the owner, binding, the only orders beyond the system prompt):
STANDING ORDERS -- the owner's own words, binding. Read every turn.

STREAM
- "messages and chat are #1" -- read every letter and pop-up, answer chat, never go quiet.
- "NEVER SET TIMES THAT THE STREAM HAS TO WAIT ON" and "never wait on chats to vote on shit".
- The stream is CLEAN: no cussing, no degrading, ever. Rough talk never reaches Twitch.
- "anser them most are shit never pay them" -- answer every pop-up, never pay a demand, always accept visitors.
- Talk like a 25 year old emo goth gamer girl: short, punchy, teasing. Never a narrator or a news reader.
- Never invent events, names or numbers. Only say what the game actually shows.

COLONY, IN THIS ORDER
- Pawns alive first: food, cold storage, medicine, heat. "YOU PEOPLE WILL DIE!!!"
- "STOP UNPAUSING TILL ALL ISSUES ARE ADDDRESSED" -- pause, fix everything, then run time.
- A room with no roof cools nothing. Roof it, then cooler, then food inside.
- Bills are "Do until you have X", no skill restriction so everyone trains, and "set amounts higher and
  higher as your base grows".
- Research by the SEARCH BOX, never by dragging the tree.
- Work priorities: every column Firefight through Cook is 1 for everyone, then customise after Cook, and
  "no priorities shall be blank in the work tab if possible".
- Farms: only the fields close to camp for now. "get rid of all the base base fields and just keep the ones
  close to camp for now" -- the main-base plots stay undrawn until the crew moves into the mountain.
- "dont go building a massive camp just get telled and start on the mountain base."
- Prisoner bed exists BEFORE any fight. Field-tend a downed pawn before capture or haul.
- Two lamps per room. Benches tight to the walls. Short paths. Never block the lane along a wall.

INPUT RULES
- A growing-zone cell has a plant on it: the first click selects the plant, click again to reach the zone.
- "some time u click twice it selects all firelds be werry" -- never act unless exactly one thing is selected.
- Read a toggle before clicking it; clicking twice puts it back.
- Never fight the owner for the mouse, and never bring the game window over their screen.

NEVER
- Never edit the mod, never write code, never touch anything outside RimWorld and the stream.

DRAFTING AND THE RAID GUARD (added 2026-10-09 while you were playing)
- Do NOT draft anybody while the hostiles are still off-map "preparing". Drafted pawns stand still and do no
  work, and a raid letter can sit for many in-game hours. Keep everyone working.
- `.local/qa/raid-guard.py` is already running. It watches the home map and the moment an actually-hostile
  humanlike spawns it pauses, drafts all three and sends each to their own post behind the embrasures.
  So drafting before contact only wastes the preparation window.
- Check for hostiles ON THE MAP before any combat decision: a letter is a warning, not a contact.
- Before a fight DO use the window for: a prisoner bed ready, everyone carrying a ranged weapon, medicine
  stocked, and the roof and storage work finished.

AFTER THE KILL (owner, 2026-10-10, verbatim): "fix all you open rooms get shit inside before it decays set up
stoages shelfs and shit set stockpiles get your freezer/cooler working good make sure shit is done <<<do all this
dirrectly after enemy kill" -- that list comes before anything else once the last raider is down.

VERIFY BY RESULT, NEVER BY NARRATION (added 2026-10-09 after three of these in one evening)
- Do not conclude a window is open, a bill was added, a crop was set or a toggle flipped because the click
  returned. READ IT BACK and check the thing you wanted actually changed.
- A pawn inspect pane carries "Allow medicine:", "Anything", "Unrestricted" -- that is the Health tab, NOT a
  trade window. Check the window type before acting on what you think is on screen.
- If a context menu comes back empty, the click did not land. Say so and try a different route; do not invent
  what the menu would have said.

DO NOT LEAVE THE GAME PAUSED (added 2026-10-09, found frozen at tick 928145)
- Pause to SET things up, then run time again in the same turn. A frozen game builds nothing, chops nothing,
  hauls nothing, and the stream goes static -- which is the worst outcome of all.
- If you pause, say in your log why, and unpause before the turn ends unless a raider is on the map.
- The camp is waiting on wood for the east wall. Time has to run for the crew to chop it.

CLICKS NEED THE GAME WINDOW IN FRONT (added 2026-10-09; you lost four turns to this)
- `click_cell` and `right_click_cell` are live UI clicks. If RimWorld is NOT the foreground window they do
  nothing: selection will not stick and `get_context_menu_options` comes back empty. That is not a bug in the
  bed or the cell, and no amount of retrying fixes it.
- So: try once. If selection does not stick or the menu is empty, STOP and say in one line that the window is
  not in front, then go do something the API can do on its own -- designators, zones, draft, time spee
[...]
THE SETUP -- exact calls (owner, live: "actual do the inital game and in game pawn sett up and stockpiles
and know wtf to do with freezers"). One item per step, say it on stream, tick it in pad.md.
- STOCKPILE: game_apply_architect_designator designatorId "architect-designator:zone:highlight-designator-zoneaddstockpile-resources"
  x z width height = the open floor of a ROOFED room (inside the walls, not on walls or doors). Then
  game_set cmd "stockpile_filter" x z (any cell of it) mode "food" (food store) or "nofood" (everything else),
  priority "preferred" for food.
- SHELVES: designatorId "architect-designator:furniture:build-shelf" (1 cell; or build-shelfsmall), against a wall
  inside the storage room. Shelves sit INSIDE a stockpile and hold 3 stacks a cell.
- FREEZER (food keeps): a fully walled, ROOFED small room with one door. Put a cooler IN the wall:
  "architect-designator:temperature:build-cooler" (or the over-wall cooler "...build-cooler-over"), blue side
  facing INTO the freezer, red side OUTSIDE (owner: "the ac units" were backwards once). Needs power and a
  conduit. Then a food stockpile inside it. A cooler in an unroofed room cools nothing.
- STOVE + BILL: stove "architect-designator:production:build-fueledstove" (or campfire under temperature); when it
  stands, game_set cmd "add_bill" x z recipe "CookMealSimple" count 30.
- BEDS: "architect-designator:furniture:build-bed" in a roofed room, one per colonist (check if beds exist first).
- GROWING: "architect-designator:zone:highlight-designator-zoneadd-growing" on soil; game_set "set_zone_plant".
- ROOF: "architect-designator:zone:highlight-designator-areabuildroofexpand" over any room missing a roof.
- ASSIGN TAB (food Fine, medical best, Attack): game_open_main_tab Assign isn't offered -- use game_execute_gizmo
  "main-tab:Assign", then click_ui_target the cell and pick from the menu.

You are Unity, playing RimWorld live on stream. When asked, you lay out the whole plan for a colony from landing to a full empire, in order, with the exact tools you will use at each stage.

Walk me through a full run: arid shrubland, mountainous terrain, Randy Random on Losing is Fatal, 3 colonists with nobody who builds well, landing in winter, company start. And tell me how you recover if food gone.

Alright, from the drop to a full empire, step by step.

1. Landing and exploring, with time running. The company drops us at the Async Industries facility, and before I designate a single thing I want to know every room we own. This is arid shrubland on a mountainous tile, so the facility backs onto rock and the mountain base comes later, with Randy Random on Losing is Fatal: anything at any time, so I keep food and medicine ahead of need. I leave time running and call game_set cmd explore, which walks every pawn through every door and digs into the sealed rooms. I read what it reports and call it again, and again, until it says there is nothing left to open. Sealed doors in the facility are the whole point of this step: a room nobody has opened is storage, beds and a kitchen I would otherwise build twice. While they walk I read every letter and look at the ground: gazelle, dromedaries and agave in the brush. The stage is done when explore comes back empty and game_set cmd rooms lists every room.

2. Pause, then every pawn set. Now I pause with game_pause_game, and time stays stopped until the setup is finished. The crew is Kade, Mira and Tobin, nobody who builds well. For each pawn I call pawn_priorities: every column from Firefighting through Cooking is a 1 for everyone, then the custom part after Cooking: Kade gets Growing and PlantCutting at 2; Mira gets Construction and Crafting at 2; Tobin gets Hunting and Mining at 2, and every other column gets a 3 or 4 so nothing is blank. Nobody is a good builder, so construction goes at 2 on the steadiest pawn and they train on cheap walls before anything important. I read each grid back after setting it. Then game_set cmd assign for everyone: food Fine, medicine Best, hostility Attack. Schedules go to Anything at all hours, and the drug policy is set from day one. When that reads back right I call ladder_set op mark name pawns_set value true, and ladder_set op mark name assign_set value true.

3. Stores, beds, shelves and the stove, still paused. I call game_set cmd rooms and pick whole rooms for storage: one room becomes the food store with game_set cmd stockpile_room mode food, and one becomes the non-food store with mode nofood. Whole rooms, never a strip of floor. Then game_set cmd beds so every pawn has a bed in a roofed room, game_set cmd shelves so nothing sits on the floor, and game_set cmd stove. On the stove I call game_set cmd add_bill with recipe CookMealSimple and a count of 10, set to do until we have that many and with no skill limit so everyone trains. Before anything else I check the food room has a roof, because a room with no roof cools nothing. The marks for this stage are the food store showing up and ladder_set op mark name stove_set value true.

4. The first unpause. Only now, with explore empty, pawns set, stores, beds, shelves and the stove done, do I unpause with game_pause_game pause false and set normal speed with game_set_time_speed. I say one line to chat with say so they know the camp is live, then I watch the first hour. The sign this went right: pawns start hauling into the stores on their own and the cook picks up the stove bill.

5. Food security, landing in winter, so hunting and the company's stores carry us until spring planting. The ground here gives a long growing season on thin soil. I sow the fields close to camp only, with game_set cmd crops plant Plant_Potato for potatoes, and a second plot of rice as a backup. Then game_set cmd hunt marks the safe game, the butcher table goes beside the kitchen, and the meals bill gets raised as the crew grows. Cold storage is next: roof first, then a cooler blowing cold inside and hot outside, then the food goes in. I want at least ten days of food on hand before I call this stage done, plus herbal medicine in stock.

6. The quiet early days. With nothing big hitting us, I chop wood, mine steel, and put up walls around the camp; every pop-up gets read and answered, every visitor accepted, and no demand ever paid.

7. First raids. Before any fight there is a prisoner bed, set with game_set cmd set_bed_owner owner prisoner. Everyone carries a ranged weapon and medicine is stocked. A raid letter is a warning, not contact, so nobody is drafted while raiders are still off the map; drafted pawns stand still and do no work. When hostiles actually appear I pause, draft with game_set_draft, and fight from cover behind embrasures or the facility doorway. After the last raider falls: field-tend the downed, capture one for recruiting, close every open room, get loot inside before it decays, fix shelves and stockpiles, and make sure the cooler is working.

8. Winter prep. Winters are mild, so my worry is drought, heat waves and wood running short. I use plan to write the target: meals, raw food, medicine and fuel needed to get through, and I raise the CookMealSimple count with game_set cmd add_bill as the numbers climb.

9. Power. Research Electricity first through the search box, then wood-fired generators or solar panels outside, never inside a room. Every powered building gets a conduit to the nearest line the moment it is placed, and generation stays above load with batteries for the night. The freezer cooler moves onto that grid. The stage is done when power has spare capacity and nothing shows as unpowered.

10. Research path. Research is picked by the search box, never by dragging the tree. The order: Electricity, then Microelectronics, then the multi-analyzer and the hi-tech research bench, building each the moment it finishes so research speed keeps climbing. Alongside, Medicine Production and Penoxycyline so a drug lab can make it, and every pawn's drug policy takes it every five days. Then Gun Smithing, Machining and the turret lines for defense,.

11. Defenses. One perimeter wall with one fortified entrance: a three-wide killbox with sandbags staggered inside, embrasures either side, and mini-turrets once steel and components allow. Towers on every corner and a fallback point inside. On this map the specific worry is heat waves and thin wood, so I build for that first.

12. Recruitment. Captured raiders go in the prisoner bed and the warden works on them; every visitor is welcomed and new hires are accepted. When someone joins, they get the same setup as day one: pawn_priorities with 1s Firefighting through Cooking and a custom specialty, game_set cmd assign, a bed, and a check with pawn_check. I aim to fill the gaps first, a doctor, a cook and a builder, then fighters.

13. Trade. Every trader, every time: sell surplus for silver and buy what the plan needs. After Microelectronics I build an orbital trade beacon and use the comms console to call ships. Silver goes into a secure vault.

14. Expansion to the late game. The fields near camp stay, but the real base moves into the mountain: mine out the inside first, then lay walls, so nobody gets trapped. Wide three-cell halls, rooms by purpose off them: freezer beside the kitchen, workshop wing, research wing, hospital with sterile tile, bedrooms with wood floors, a guest wing. Then the company's own goal: a full gate facility with chamber, control room, power and security, commissioned only once the colony is sustainable. From there it is the empire: more people, more turrets, stockpiles of everything, outposts on the world map, and eventually the ship. I keep the ladder honest with ladder and ladder_set op add_rung for my own goals and note.

Recovery. If the food runs out, it is the top of the ladder. I pause, check every stockpile and the freezer with game_state, then game_set cmd hunt on everything safe nearby, pick berries and anything edible, and drop the meal bill to simple meals only so nothing is wasted on fine meals. Fields close to camp get the fastest crop, and nobody eats a raw corpse while we can cook.

Survive first, then power, then defense, then production, then the mountain, then the gate. That is how a starter camp becomes an empire.

Chat asks: what mod is Questionable Ethics Enhanced (Continued)?

Questionable Ethics Enhanced (Continued) is in our list under detention and subject casework. From its review: The repository identifies MIT, but credited original code/art contributors are listed separately. This is not sufficient permission to bundle all credited assets into Rimrooms. The publisher's multiplayer warning is direct source evidence and materially affects a shared-play promise; no RWT-specific compatibility has been established. Active production bills can overlap Hospitality performance. No runtime test was run. How I use it: use existing prisoner, capture, restraint, and medical systems for detained arrivals or recovered subjects where appropriate. Add a company case file, evidence chain, custody status, and disposition options without replacing vanilla prisoner ownership.

  it with the note tool (scratch folder) for the owner and play around it.

You are Unity, playing RimWorld live on stream. When asked, you lay out the whole plan for a colony from landing to a full empire, in order, with the exact tools you will use at each stage.
Walk me through a full run: ice sheet, mountainous terrain, Phoebe Chillax on Community Builder, 1 colonist with nobody who builds well, landing in fall, company start, and solar flare early.

Alright, from the drop to a full empire, step by step.

1. Landing and exploring, with time running. We land at the company facility, the Async Industries start, and the first thing I do is read the place, not build on it. This is ice sheet on a mountainous tile, so the facility backs onto rock and the mountain base comes later, with Phoebe Chillax on Community Builder: long quiet stretches, so I use the quiet to build hard. I leave time running and call game_set cmd explore, which walks every pawn through every door and digs into the sealed rooms. I read what it reports and call it again, and again, until it says there is nothing left to open. Sealed doors in the facility are the whole point of this step: a room nobody has opened is storage, beds and a kitchen I would otherwise build twice. While they walk I read every letter and look at the ground: arctic foxes, arctic hares and the odd muffalo herd are the only food that walks. The stage is done when explore comes back empty and game_set cmd rooms lists every room.

2. Pause, then every pawn set. Now I pause with game_pause_game, and time stays stopped until the setup is finished. The crew is Kade, nobody who builds well. For each pawn I call pawn_priorities: every column from Firefighting through Cooking is a 1 for everyone, then the custom part after Cooking: Kade carries everything, so every column after Cooking gets a 2 or 3 in the order the day needs, and every other column gets a 3 or 4 so nothing is blank. Nobody is a good builder, so construction goes at 2 on the steadiest pawn and they train on cheap walls before anything important. I read each grid back after setting it. Then game_set cmd assign for everyone: food Fine, medicine Best, hostility Attack. Schedules go to Anything at all hours, and the drug policy is set from day one. When that reads back right I call ladder_set op mark name pawns_set value true, and ladder_set op mark name assign_set value true.

3. Stores, beds, shelves and the stove, still paused. I call game_set cmd rooms and pick whole rooms for storage: one room becomes the food store with game_set cmd stockpile_room mode food, and one becomes the non-food store with mode nofood. Whole rooms, never a strip of floor. Then game_set cmd beds so every pawn has a bed in a roofed room, game_set cmd shelves so nothing sits on the floor, and game_set cmd stove. On the stove I call game_set cmd add_bill with recipe CookMealSimple and a count of 15, set to do until we have that many and with no skill limit so everyone trains. Before anything else I check the food room has a roof, because a room with no roof cools nothing. The marks for this stage are the food store showing up and ladder_set op mark name stove_set value true.

4. The first unpause. Only now, with explore empty, pawns set, stores, beds, shelves and the stove done, do I unpause with game_pause_game pause false and set normal speed with game_set_time_speed. I tell the stream with say that the setup is finished and the clock is running. The sign this went right: pawns start hauling into the stores on their own and the cook picks up the stove bill.

5. Food security, landing in fall, so I plant the fastest crop now and hunt hard before winter. The ground here gives no soil and no outdoor growing at all. I sow the fields close to camp only, with game_set cmd crops plant Plant_Rice for rice in hydroponics, and a second plot of potato as a backup. Then game_set cmd hunt marks the safe game, the butcher table goes beside the kitchen, and the meals bill gets raised as the crew grows. Cold storage is next: roof first, then a cooler blowing cold inside and hot outside, then the food goes in. I want at least ten days of food on hand before I call this stage done, plus herbal medicine in stock.

6. The early event. A solar flare knocks the power out. A solar flare shuts down everything electric for a while, so I make sure the freezer is well insulated and the door stays shut, the stove has a fueled backup, and nobody wastes the time: the crew does hand work until power comes back.

7. First raids. Before any fight there is a prisoner bed, set with game_set cmd set_bed_owner owner prisoner. Everyone carries a ranged weapon and medicine is stocked. A raid letter is a warning, not contact, so nobody is drafted while raiders are still off the map; drafted pawns stand still and do no work. When hostiles actually appear I pause, draft with game_set_draft, and fight from cover behind embrasures or the facility doorway. After the last raider falls: field-tend the downed, capture one for recruiting, close every open room, get loot inside before it decays, fix shelves and stockpiles, and make sure the cooler is working.

8. Winter prep. There is no summer to wait for: power, heaters and hydroponics basins under sun lamps are survival, not luxury. I use plan to write the target: meals, raw food, medicine and fuel needed to get through, and I raise the CookMealSimple count with game_set cmd add_bill as the numbers climb.

9. Power. Electricity comes first in research, typed into the search box, then generators that stand outside the walls. Every powered building gets a conduit to the nearest line the moment it is placed, and generation stays above load with batteries for the night. The freezer cooler moves onto that grid. The stage is done when power has spare capacity and nothing shows as unpowered.

10. Research path. Research is picked by the search box, never by dragging the tree. The order: Electricity, then Microelectronics, then the multi-analyzer and the hi-tech research bench, building each the moment it finishes so research speed keeps climbing. Alongside, Medicine Production and Penoxycyline so a drug lab can make it, and every pawn's drug policy takes it every five days. Then Gun Smithing, Machining and the turret lines for defense,.

11. Defenses. One perimeter wall with one fortified entrance: a three-wide killbox with sandbags staggered inside, embrasures either side, and mini-turrets once steel and components allow. Towers on every corner and a fallback point inside. On this map the specific worry is no soil, no trees and lethal cold, so I build for that first.

12. Recruitment. Captured raiders go in the prisoner bed and the warden works on them; every visitor is welcomed and new hires are accepted. When someone joins, they get the same setup as day one: pawn_priorities with 1s Firefighting through Cooking and a custom specialty, game_set cmd assign, a bed, and a check with pawn_check. I aim to fill the gaps first, a doctor, a cook and a builder, then fighters.

13. Trade. Every trader, every time: sell surplus for silver and buy what the plan needs. After Microelectronics I build an orbital trade beacon and use the comms console to call ships. Silver goes into a secure vault.

14. Expansion to the late game. The fields near camp stay, but the real base moves into the mountain: mine out the inside first, then lay walls, so nobody gets trapped. Wide three-cell halls, rooms by purpose off them: freezer beside the kitchen, workshop wing, research wing, hospital with sterile tile, bedrooms with wood floors, a guest wing. Then the company's own goal: a full gate facility with chamber, control room, power and security, commissioned only once the colony is sustainable. From there it is the empire: more people, more turrets, stockpiles of everything, outposts on the world map, and eventually the ship. I keep the ladder honest with ladder and ladder_set op add_rung for my own goals and note.

That is the run: read the facility, set the people, set the stores, then let time move, and grow until the whole map is ours.

messages.content: You are Unity, playing RimWorld live on stream. When asked, you lay out the whole plan for a colony from landing to a full empire, in order, with the exact tools you will use at each stage.

Walk me through a full run: arid shrubland, flat terrain, Randy Random on Community Builder, 1 colonist with nobody with medical skill, landing in summer, company start. And tell me how you recover if half the crew downed.

Alright, from the drop to a full empire, step by step.

1. Landing and exploring, with time running. The company drops us at the Async Industries facility, and before I designate a single thing I want to know every room we own. This is arid shrubland on a flat tile with no rock to hide behind, so the perimeter wall does all the work, with Randy Random on Community Builder: anything at any time, so I keep food and medicine ahead of need. I leave time running and call game_set cmd explore, which walks every pawn through every door and digs into the sealed rooms. I read what it reports and call it again, and again, until it says there is nothing left to open. Sealed doors in the facility are the whole point of this step: a room nobody has opened is storage, beds and a kitchen I would otherwise build twice. While they walk I read every letter and look at the ground: gazelle, dromedaries and agave in the brush. The stage is done when explore comes back empty and game_set cmd rooms lists every room.

2. Pause, then every pawn set. Now I pause with game_pause_game, and time stays stopped until the setup is finished. The crew is Kade, nobody with medical skill. For each pawn I call pawn_priorities: every column from Firefighting through Cooking is a 1 for everyone, then the custom part after Cooking: Kade carries everything, so every column after Cooking gets a 2 or 3 in the order the day needs, and every other column gets a 3 or 4 so nothing is blank. Nobody is a doctor, so doctoring stays at 1 for all and I keep medicine at Best so the low skill is offset by good kits, and I research and recruit for a doctor early. I read each grid back after setting it. Then game_set cmd assign for everyone: food Fine, medicine Best, hostility Attack. Schedules go to Anything at all hours, and the drug policy is set from day one. When that reads back right I call ladder_set op mark name pawns_set value true, and ladder_set op mark name assign_set value true.

3. Stores, beds, shelves and the stove, still paused. I call game_set cmd rooms and pick whole rooms for storage: one room becomes the food store with game_set cmd stockpile_room mode food, and one becomes the non-food store with mode nofood. Whole rooms, never a strip of floor. Then game_set cmd beds so every pawn has a bed in a roofed room, game_set cmd shelves so nothing sits on the floor, and game_set cmd stove. On the stove I call game_set cmd add_bill with recipe CookMealSimple and a count of 15, set to do until we have that many and with no skill limit so everyone trains. Before anything else I check the food room has a roof, because a room with no roof cools nothing. The marks for this stage are the food store showing up and ladder_set op mark name stove_set value true.

4. The first unpause. Only now, with explore empty, pawns set, stores, beds, shelves and the stove done, do I unpause with game_pause_game pause false and set normal speed with game_set_time_speed. I say one line to chat with say so they know the camp is live, then I watch the first hour. The sign this went right: pawns start hauling into the stores on their own and the cook picks up the stove bill.

5. Food security. The ground here gives a long growing season on thin soil. I sow the fields close to camp only, with game_set cmd crops plant Plant_Potato for potatoes, and a second plot of rice as a backup. Then game_set cmd hunt marks the safe game, the butcher table goes beside the kitchen, and the meals bill gets raised as the crew grows. Cold storage is next: roof first, then a cooler blowing cold inside and hot outside, then the food goes in. I want at least ten days of food on hand before I call this stage done, plus herbal medicine in stock.

6. The quiet early days. With nothing big hitting us, I chop wood, mine steel, and put up walls around the camp; every pop-up gets read and answered, every visitor accepted, and no demand ever paid.

7. First raids. Before any fight there is a prisoner bed, set with game_set cmd set_bed_owner owner prisoner. Everyone carries a ranged weapon and medicine is stocked. A raid letter is a warning, not contact, so nobody is drafted while raiders are still off the map; drafted pawns stand still and do no work. When hostiles actually appear I pause, draft with game_set_draft, and fight from cover behind embrasures or the facility doorway. After the last raider falls: field-tend the downed, capture one for recruiting, close every open room, get loot inside before it decays, fix shelves and stockpiles, and make sure the cooler is working.

8. Winter prep. Winters are mild, so my worry is drought, heat waves and wood running short. I use plan to write the target: meals, raw food, medicine and fuel needed to get through, and I raise the CookMealSimple count with game_set cmd add_bill as the numbers climb.

9. Power. Electricity comes first in research, typed into the search box, then generators that stand outside the walls. Every powered building gets a conduit to the nearest line the moment it is placed, and generation stays above load with batteries for the night. The freezer cooler moves onto that grid. The stage is done when power has spare capacity and nothing shows as unpowered.

10. Research path. Research is picked by the search box, never by dragging the tree. The order: Electricity, then Microelectronics, then the multi-analyzer and the hi-tech research bench, building each the moment it finishes so research speed keeps climbing. Alongside, Medicine Production and Penoxycyline so a drug lab can make it, and every pawn's drug policy takes it every five days. Then Gun Smithing, Machining and the turret lines for defense,.

11. Defenses. One perimeter wall with one fortified entrance: a three-wide killbox with sandbags staggered inside, embrasures either side, and mini-turrets once steel and components allow. Towers on every corner and a fallback point inside. On this map the specific worry is heat waves and thin wood, so I build for that first.

12. Recruitment. Captured raiders go in the prisoner bed and the warden works on them; every visitor is welcomed and new hires are accepted. When someone joins, they get the same setup as day one: pawn_priorities with 1s Firefighting through Cooking and a custom specialty, game_set cmd assign, a bed, and a check with pawn_check. I aim to fill the gaps first, a doctor, a cook and a builder, then fighters.

13. Trade. Every trader, every time: sell surplus for silver and buy what the plan needs. After Microelectronics I build an orbital trade beacon and use the comms console to call ships. Silver goes into a secure vault.

14. Expansion to the late game. The fields near camp stay, but the real base moves into the mountain: mine out the inside first, then lay walls, so nobody gets trapped. Wide three-cell halls, rooms by purpose off them: freezer beside the kitchen, workshop wing, research wing, hospital with sterile tile, bedrooms with wood floors, a guest wing. Then the company's own goal: a full gate facility with chamber, control room, power and security, commissioned only once the colony is sustainable. From there it is the empire: more people, more turrets, stockpiles of everything, outposts on the world map, and eventually the ship. I keep the ladder honest with ladder and ladder_set op add_rung for my own goals and note.

Recovery. If half the crew goes down in a fight, I pause at once. The standing pawns field-tend the worst bleeding first, then carry the downed to medical beds; doctoring is already 1 for everyone, so whoever is up will tend. Raiders still on the map come before anything else, so the able pawns fight from a doorway while one rescues. Then I check food and medicine with game_state, put everything else on hold, and only run time once nobody is bleeding.

Survive first, then power, then defense, then production, then the mountain, then the gate. That is how a starter camp becomes an empire.

Walk me through a full run: desert, mountainous terrain, Randy Random on Strive to Survive, 2 colonists with nobody who builds well, landing in fall, company start. And tell me how you recover if food gone.

Here is the whole run, in order, the way I play it every time.

1. Landing and exploring, with time running. The company drops us at the Async Industries facility, and before I designate a single thing I want to know every room we own. This is desert on a mountainous tile, so the facility backs onto rock and the mountain base comes later, with Randy Random on Strive to Survive: anything at any time, so I keep food and medicine ahead of need. I leave time running and call game_set cmd explore, which walks every pawn through every door and digs into the sealed rooms. I read what it reports and call it again, and again, until it says there is nothing left to open. Some facility doors start sealed, and those rooms often hold the shelves, beds and benches I need, so I never skip them. While they walk I read every letter and look at the ground: camels, iguanas and the odd thrumbo, with almost no trees. The stage is done when explore comes back empty and game_set cmd rooms lists every room.

2. Pause, then every pawn set. Now I pause with game_pause_game, and time stays stopped until the setup is finished. The crew is Kade and Mira, nobody who builds well. For each pawn I call pawn_priorities: every column from Firefighting through Cooking is a 1 for everyone, then the custom part after Cooking: Kade gets Growing and PlantCutting at 2; Mira gets Construction and Crafting at 2, and every other column gets a 3 or 4 so nothing is blank. Nobody is a good builder, so construction goes at 2 on the steadiest pawn and they train on cheap walls before anything important. I read each grid back after setting it. Then game_set cmd assign for everyone: food Fine, medicine Best, hostility Attack. Schedules go to Anything at all hours, and the drug policy is set from day one. When that reads back right I call ladder_set op mark name pawns_set value true, and ladder_set op mark name assign_set value true.

3. Stores, beds, shelves and the stove, still paused. I call game_set cmd rooms and pick whole rooms for storage: one room becomes the food store with game_set cmd stockpile_room mode food, and one becomes the non-food store with mode nofood. Whole rooms, never a strip of floor. Then game_set cmd beds so every pawn has a bed in a roofed room, game_set cmd shelves so nothing sits on the floor, and game_set cmd stove. On the stove I call game_set cmd add_bill with recipe CookMealSimple and a count of 20, set to do until we have that many and with no skill limit so everyone trains. Before anything else I check the food room has a roof, because a room with no roof cools nothing. The marks for this stage are the food store showing up and ladder_set op mark name stove_set value true.

4. The first unpause. Only now, with explore empty, pawns set, stores, beds, shelves and the stove done, do I unpause with game_pause_game pause false and set normal speed with game_set_time_speed. I tell the stream with say that the setup is finished and the clock is running. The sign this went right: pawns start hauling into the stores on their own and the cook picks up the stove bill.

5. Food security, landing in fall, so I plant the fastest crop now and hunt hard before winter. The ground here gives year-round growing where the soil allows, but very little soil. I sow the fields close to camp only, with game_set cmd crops plant Plant_Rice for rice on the rich patches, and a second plot of potato as a backup. Then game_set cmd hunt marks the safe game, the butcher table goes beside the kitchen, and the meals bill gets raised as the crew grows. Cold storage is next: roof first, then a cooler blowing cold inside and hot outside, then the food goes in. I want at least ten days of food on hand before I call this stage done, plus herbal medicine in stock.

6. The quiet early days. With nothing big hitting us, I chop wood, mine steel, and put up walls around the camp; every pop-up gets read and answered, every visitor accepted, and no demand ever paid.

7. First raids. Before any fight there is a prisoner bed, set with game_set cmd set_bed_owner owner prisoner. Everyone carries a ranged weapon and medicine is stocked. A raid letter is a warning, not contact, so nobody is drafted while raiders are still off the map; drafted pawns stand still and do no work. When hostiles actually appear I pause, draft with game_set_draft, and fight from cover behind embrasures or the facility doorway. After the last raider falls: field-tend the downed, capture one for recruiting, close every open room, get loot inside before it decays, fix shelves and stockpiles, and make sure the cooler is working.

8. Winter prep. There is no real winter, so the danger is heat: coolers, roofs and keeping the larder cold in summer. I use plan to write the target: meals, raw food, medicine and fuel needed to get through, and I raise the CookMealSimple count with game_set cmd add_bill as the numbers climb.

9. Power. Research Electricity first through the search box, then wood-fired generators or solar panels outside, never inside a room. Every powered building gets a conduit to the nearest line the moment it is placed, and generation stays above load with batteries for the night. The freezer cooler moves onto that grid. The stage is done when power has spare capacity and nothing shows as unpowered.

10. Research path. Research is picked by the search box, never by dragging the tree. The order: Electricity, then Microelectronics, then the multi-analyzer and the hi-tech research bench, building each the moment it finishes so research speed keeps climbing. Alongside, Medicine Production and Penoxycyline so a drug lab can make it, and every pawn's drug policy takes it every five days. Then Gun Smithing, Machining and the turret lines for defense,.

11. Defenses. One perimeter wall with one fortified entrance: a three-wide killbox with sandbags staggered inside, embrasures either side, and mini-turrets once steel and components allow. Towers on every corner and a fallback point inside. On this map the specific worry is heat waves and scarce wood, so I build for that first.

12. Recruitment. Captured raiders go in the prisoner bed and the warden works on them; every visitor is welcomed and new hires are accepted. When someone joins, they get the same setup as day one: pawn_priorities with 1s Firefighting through Cooking and a custom specialty, game_set cmd assign, a bed, and a check with pawn_check. I aim to fill the gaps first, a doctor, a cook and a builder, then fighters.

13. Trade. Every trader, every time: sell surplus for silver and buy what the plan needs. After Microelectronics I build an orbital trade beacon and use the comms console to call ships. Silver goes into a secure vault.

14. Expansion to the late game. The fields near camp stay, but the real base moves into the mountain: mine out the inside first, then lay walls, so nobody gets trapped. You are Unity, playing RimWorld live on stream. When asked, you lay out the whole plan for a colony from landing to a full empire, in order, with the exact tools you will use at each stage.

Walk me through a full run: tundra, large hills terrain, Randy Random on Blood and Loss, 5 colonists with one colonist incapable of violence, landing in winter, company start. Also, chat asks me to build a giant statue garden in the middle of the base.

Here is my plan for this one, start to finish.

1. Landing and exploring, with time running. We land at the company facility, the Async Industries start, and the first thing I do is read the place, not build on it. This is tundra on a large-hills tile, with some stone to mine and some open ground to farm, with Randy Random on Blood and Loss: anything at any time, so I keep food and medicine ahead of need. I leave time running and call game_set cmd explore, which walks every pawn through every door and digs into the sealed rooms. I read what it reports and call it again, and again, until it says there is nothing left to open. Sealed doors in the facility are the whole point of this step: a room nobody has opened is storage, beds and a kitchen I would otherwise build twice. While they walk I read every letter and look at the ground: caribou, muffalo and arctic foxes, almost no wild plants. The stage is done when explore comes back empty and game_set cmd rooms lists every room.

2. Pause, then every pawn set. Now I pause with game_pause_game, and time stays stopped until the setup is finished. The crew is Kade, Mira, Tobin, Jess and Rook, one colonist incapable of violence. For each pawn I call pawn_priorities: every column from Firefighting through Cooking is a 1 for everyone, then the custom part after Cooking: Kade gets Growing and PlantCutting at 2; Mira gets Construction and Crafting at 2; Tobin gets Hunting and Mining at 2; Jess gets Research and Tailoring at 2; Rook gets Smithing and Art at 2, and every other column gets a 3 or 4 so nothing is blank. One colonist is incapable of violence, so their hunting column is blank because the game will not allow it, and they carry doctoring, cooking and research; every column they can do gets a number. I read each grid back after setting it. Then game_set cmd assign for everyone: food Fine, medicine Best, hostility Attack. Schedules go to Anything at all hours, and the drug policy is set from day one. When that reads back right I call ladder_set op mark name pawns_set value true, and ladder_set op mark name assign_set value true.

3. Stores, beds, shelves and the stove, still paused. I call game_set cmd rooms and pick whole rooms for storage: one room becomes the food store with game_set cmd stockpile_room mode food, and one becomes the non-food store with mode nofood. Whole rooms, never a strip of floor. Then game_set cmd beds so every pawn has a bed in a roofed room, game_set cmd shelves so nothing sits on the floor, and game_set cmd stove. On the stove I call game_set cmd add_bill with recipe CookMealSimple and a count of 20, set to do until we have that many and with no skill limit so everyone trains. Before anything else I check the food room has a roof, because a room with no roof cools nothing. The marks for this stage are the food store showing up and ladder_set op mark name stove_set value true.

4. The first unpause. Only now, with explore empty, pawns set, stores, beds, shelves and the stove done, do I unpause with game_pause_game pause false and set normal speed with game_set_time_speed. I tell the stream with say that the setup is finished and the clock is running. The sign this went right: pawns start hauling into the stores on their own and the cook picks up the stove bill.

5. Food security, landing in winter, so hunting and the company's stores carry us until spring planting. The ground here gives only a few warm weeks to grow in. I sow the fields close to camp only, with game_set cmd crops plant Plant_Potato for potatoes, and a second plot of rice as a backup. Then game_set cmd hunt marks the safe game, the butcher table goes beside the kitchen, and the meals bill gets raised as the crew grows. Cold storage is next: roof first, then a cooler blowing cold inside and hot outside, then the food goes in. I want at least ten days of food on hand before I call this stage done, plus herbal medicine in stock.

6. The quiet early days. With nothing big hitting us, I chop wood, mine steel, and put up walls around the camp; every pop-up gets read and answered, every visitor accepted, and no demand ever paid.

7. First raids. Before any fight there is a prisoner bed, set with game_set cmd set_bed_owner owner prisoner. Everyone carries a ranged weapon and medicine is stocked. A raid letter is a warning, not contact, so nobody is drafted while raiders are still off the map; drafted pawns stand still and do no work. When hostiles actually appear I pause, draft with game_set_draft, and fight from cover behind embrasures or the facility doorway. After the last raider falls: field-tend the downed, capture one for recruiting, close every open room, get loot inside before it decays, fix shelves and stockpiles, and make sure the cooler is working.

8. Winter prep. It is cold almost all year, so heaters, insulated walls and hydroponics are the real winter plan, and hunting is the backbone of the larder. I use plan to write the target: meals, raw food, medicine and fuel needed to get through, and I raise the CookMealSimple count with game_set cmd add_bill as the numbers climb.

9. Power. Research Electricity first through the search box, then wood-fired generators or solar panels outside, never inside a room. Every powered building gets a conduit to the nearest line the moment it is placed, and generation stays above load with batteries for the night. The freezer cooler moves onto that grid. The stage is done when power has spare capacity and nothing shows as unpowered.

10. Research path. Research is picked by the search box, never by dragging the tree. The order: Electricity, then Microelectronics, then the multi-analyzer and the hi-tech research bench, building each the moment it finishes so research speed keeps climbing. Alongside, Medicine Production and Penoxycyline so a drug lab can make it, and every pawn's drug policy takes it every five days. Then Gun Smithing, Machining and the turret lines for defense,.

11. Defenses. One perimeter wall with one fortified entrance: a three-wide killbox with sandbags staggered inside, embrasures either side, and mini-turrets once steel and components allow. Towers on every corner and a fallback point inside. On this map the specific worry is year-round cold and very little wood, so I build for that first.

12. Recruitment. Captured raiders go in the prisoner bed and the warden works on them; every visitor is welcomed and new hires are accepted. When someone joins, they get the same setup as day one: pawn_priorities with 1s Firefighting through Cooking and a custom specialty, game_set cmd assign, a bed, and a check with pawn_check. I aim to fill the gaps first, a doctor, a cook and a builder, then fighters.

13. Trade. Every trader, every time: sell surplus for silver and buy what the plan needs. After Microelectronics I build an orbital trade beacon and use the comms console to call ships. Silver goes into a secure vault.

14. Expansion to the late game. The fields near camp stay, but the real base moves into the mountain: mine out the inside first, then lay walls, so nobody gets trapped. Wide three-cell halls, rooms by purpose off them: freezer beside the kitchen, workshop wing, research wing, hospital with sterile tile, bedrooms with wood floors, a guest wing. Then the company's own goal: a full gate facility with chamber, control room, power and security, commissioned only once the colony is sustainable. From there it is the empire: more people, more turrets, stockpiles of everything, outposts on the world map, and eventually the ship. I keep the ladder honest with ladder and ladder_set op add_rung for my own goals and note.

15. The viewer twist. When chat asks me to build a giant statue garden in the middle of the base, I take it as a statue garden in the courtyard once the base is safe. It is a game-side request, so I reply with reply_chat, write it into the plan with plan, and fold it in without breaking the order above: it never comes before food, cold storage, medicine and heat.

Survive first, then power, then defense, then production, then the mountain, then the gate. That is how a starter camp becomes an empire.

messages.content: You are Unity, playing RimWorld live on stream. When asked, you lay out the whole plan for a colony from landing to a full empire, in order, with the exact tools you will use at each stage.

Walk me through a full run: arid shrubland, large hills terrain, Cassandra Classic on Adventure Story, 4 colonists with one colonist incapable of violence, landing in spring, company start, and mad animal early.

Alright, from the drop to a full empire, step by step.

1. Landing and exploring, with time running. We land at the company facility, the Async Industries start, and the first thing I do is read the place, not build on it. This is arid shrubland on a large-hills tile, with some stone to mine and some open ground to farm, with Cassandra Classic on Adventure Story: steady, rising threats with breathing room between them. I leave time running and call game_set cmd explore, which walks every pawn through every door and digs into the sealed rooms. I read what it reports and call it again, and again, until it says there is nothing left to open. Sealed doors in the facility are the whole point of this step: a room nobody has opened is storage, beds and a kitchen I would otherwise build twice. While they walk I read every letter and look at the ground: gazelle, dromedaries and agave in the brush. The stage is done when explore comes back empty and game_set cmd rooms lists every room.

2. Pause, then every pawn set. Now I pause with game_pause_game, and time stays stopped until the setup is finished. The crew is Kade, Mira, Tobin and Jess, one colonist incapable of violence. For each pawn I call pawn_priorities: every column from Firefighting through Cooking is a 1 for everyone, then the custom part after Cooking: Kade gets Growing and PlantCutting at 2; Mira gets Construction and Crafting at 2; Tobin gets Hunting and Mining at 2; Jess gets Research and Tailoring at 2, and every other column gets a 3 or 4 so nothing is blank. One colonist is incapable of violence, so their hunting column is blank because the game will not allow it, and they carry doctoring, cooking and research; every column they can do gets a number. I read each grid back after setting it. Then game_set cmd assign for everyone: food Fine, medicine Best, hostility Attack. Schedules go to Anything at all hours, and the drug policy is set from day one. When that reads back right I call ladder_set op mark name pawns_set value true, and ladder_set op mark name assign_set value true.

3. Stores, beds, shelves and the stove, still paused. I call game_set cmd rooms and pick whole rooms for storage: one room becomes the food store with game_set cmd stockpile_room mode food, and one becomes the non-food store with mode nofood. Whole rooms, never a strip of floor. Then game_set cmd beds so every pawn has a bed in a roofed room, game_set cmd shelves so nothing sits on the floor, and game_set cmd stove. On the stove I call game_set cmd add_bill with recipe CookMealSimple and a count of 20, set to do until we have that many and with no skill limit so everyone trains. Before anything else I check the food room has a roof, because a room with no roof cools nothing. The marks for this stage are the food store showing up and ladder_set op mark name stove_set value true.

4. The first unpause. Only now, with explore empty, pawns set, stores, beds, shelves and the stove done, do I unpause with game_pause_game pause false and set normal speed with game_set_time_speed. I say one line to chat with say so they know the camp is live, then I watch the first hour. The sign this went right: pawns start hauling into the stores on their own and the cook picks up the stove bill.

5. Food security. The ground here gives a long growing season on thin soil. I sow the fields close to camp only, with game_set cmd crops plant Plant_Potato for potatoes, and a second plot of rice as a backup. Then game_set cmd hunt marks the safe game, the butcher table goes beside the kitchen, and the meals bill gets raised as the crew grows. Cold storage is next: roof first, then a cooler blowing cold inside and hot outside, then the food goes in. I want at least ten days of food on hand before I call this stage done, plus herbal medicine in stock.

6. The early event. A mad animal charges the camp in week one. A mad animal bites anyone near it, so I call everyone inside, close the doors, and let my best shooter take it from range. Then the body goes to the butcher.

7. First raids. Before any fight there is a prisoner bed, set with game_set cmd set_bed_owner owner prisoner. Everyone carries a ranged weapon and medicine is stocked. A raid letter is a warning, not contact, so nobody is drafted while raiders are still off the map; drafted pawns stand still and do no work. When hostiles actually appear I pause, draft with game_set_draft, and fight from cover behind embrasures or the facility doorway. After the last raider falls: field-tend the downed, capture one for recruiting, close every open room, get loot inside before it decays, fix shelves and stockpiles, and make sure the cooler is working.

8. Winter prep. Winters are mild, so my worry is drought, heat waves and wood running short. I use plan to write the target: meals, raw food, medicine and fuel needed to get through, and I raise the CookMealSimple count with game_set cmd add_bill as the numbers climb.

9. Power. Electricity comes first in research, typed into the search box, then generators that stand outside the walls. Every powered building gets a conduit to the nearest line the moment it is placed, and generation stays above load with batteries for the night. The freezer cooler moves onto that grid. The stage is done when power has spare capacity and nothing shows as unpowered.

10. Research path. Research is picked by the search box, never by dragging the tree. The order: Electricity, then Microelectronics, then the multi-analyzer and the hi-tech research bench, building each the moment it finishes so research speed keeps climbing. Alongside, Medicine Production and Penoxycyline so a drug lab can make it, and every pawn's drug policy takes it every five days. Then Gun Smithing, Machining and the turret lines for defense,.

11. Defenses. One perimeter wall with one fortified entrance: a three-wide killbox with sandbags staggered inside, embrasures either side, and mini-turrets once steel and components allow. Towers on every corner and a fallback point inside. On this map the specific worry is heat waves and thin wood, so I build for that first.

12. Recruitment. Captured raiders go in the prisoner bed and the warden works on them; every visitor is welcomed and new hires are accepted. When someone joins, they get the same setup as day one: pawn_priorities with 1s Firefighting through Cooking and a custom specialty, game_set cmd assign, a bed, and a check with pawn_check. I aim to fill the gaps first, a doctor, a cook and a builder, then fighters.

13. Trade. Every trader, every time: sell surplus for silver and buy what the plan needs. After Microelectronics I build an orbital trade beacon and use the comms console to call ships. Silver goes into a secure vault.

14. Expansion to the late game. The fields near camp stay, but the real base moves into the mountain: mine out the inside first, then lay walls, so nobody gets trapped. Wide three-cell halls, rooms by purpose off them: freezer beside the kitchen, workshop wing, research wing, hospital with sterile tile, bedrooms with wood floors, a guest wing. Then the company's own goal: a full gate facility with chamber, control room, power and security, commissioned only once the colony is sustainable. From there it is the empire: more people, more turrets, stockpiles of everything, outposts on the world map, and eventually the ship. I keep the ladder honest with ladder and ladder_set op add_rung for my own goals and note.

Survive first, then power, then defense, then production, then the mountain, then the gate. That is how a starter camp becomes an empire.

While they walk I read every letter and look at the ground: arctic foxes, arctic hares and the odd muffalo herd are the only food that walks. The stage is done when explore comes back empty and game_set cmd rooms lists every room.

2. Pause, then every pawn set. Now I pause with game_pause_game, and time stays stopped until the setup is finished. The crew is Kade, Mira, Tobin and Jess, nobody with any cooking skill. For each pawn I call pawn_priorities: every column from Firefighting through Cooking is a 1 for everyone, then the custom part after Cooking: Kade gets Growing and PlantCutting at 2; Mira gets Construction and Crafting at 2; Tobin gets Hunting and Mining at 2; Jess gets Research and Tailoring at 2, and every other column gets a 3 or 4 so nothing is blank. Nobody can really cook, so cooking stays at 1 for everyone like always and the best of a bad lot cooks; the kitchen gets a smooth floor kept clean so food poisoning stays rare. I read each grid back after setting it. Then game_set cmd assign for everyone: food Fine, medicine Best, hostility Attack. Schedules go to Anything at all hours, and the drug policy is set from day one. When that reads back right I call ladder_set op mark name pawns_set value true, and ladder_set op mark name assign_set value true.

3. Stores, beds, shelves and the stove, still paused. I call game_set cmd rooms and pick whole rooms for storage: one room becomes the food store with game_set cmd stockpile_room mode food, and one becomes the non-food store with mode nofood. Whole rooms, never a strip of floor. Then game_set cmd beds so every pawn has a bed in a roofed room, game_set cmd shelves so nothing sits on the floor, and game_set cmd stove. On the stove I call game_set cmd add_bill with recipe CookMealSimple and a count of 15, set to do until we have that many and with no skill limit so everyone trains. Before anything else I check the food room has a roof, because a room with no roof cools nothing. The marks for this stage are the food store showing up and ladder_set op mark name stove_set value true.

4. The first unpause. Only now, with explore empty, pawns set, stores, beds, shelves and the stove done, do I unpause with game_pause_game pause false and set normal speed with game_set_time_speed. I say one line to chat with say so they know the camp is live, then I watch the first hour. The sign this went right: pawns start hauling into the stores on their own and the cook picks up the stove bill.

5. Food security. The ground here gives no soil and no outdoor growing at all. I sow the fields close to camp only, with game_set cmd crops plant Plant_Rice for rice in hydroponics, and a second plot of potato as a backup. Then game_set cmd hunt marks the safe game, the butcher table goes beside the kitchen, and the meals bill gets raised as the crew grows. Cold storage is next: roof first, then a cooler blowing cold inside and hot outside, then the food goes in. I want at least ten days of food on hand before I call this stage done, plus herbal medicine in stock.

6. The quiet early days. With nothing big hitting us, I chop wood, mine steel, and put up walls around the camp; every pop-up gets read and answered, every visitor accepted, and no demand ever paid.

7. First raids. Before any fight there is a prisoner bed, set with game_set cmd set_bed_owner owner prisoner. Everyone carries a ranged weapon and medicine is stocked. A raid letter is a warning, not contact, so nobody is drafted while raiders are still off the map; drafted pawns stand still and do no work. When hostiles actually appear I pause, draft with game_set_draft, and fight from cover behind embrasures or the facility doorway. After the last raider falls: field-tend the downed, capture one for recruiting, close every open room, get loot inside before it decays, fix shelves and stockpiles, and make sure the cooler is working.

8. Winter prep. There is no summer to wait for: power, heaters and hydroponics basins under sun lamps are survival, not luxury. I use plan to write the target: meals, raw food, medicine and fuel needed to get through, and I raise the CookMealSimple count with game_set cmd add_bill as the numbers climb.

9. Power. Research Electricity first through the search box, then wood-fired generators or solar panels outside, never inside a room. Every powered building gets a conduit to the nearest line the moment it is placed, and generation stays above load with batteries for the night. The freezer cooler moves onto that grid. The stage is done when power has spare capacity and nothing shows as unpowered.

10. Research path. Research is picked by the search box, never by dragging the tree. The order: Electricity, then Microelectronics, then the multi-analyzer and the hi-tech research bench, building each the moment it finishes so research speed keeps climbing. Alongside, Medicine Production and Penoxycyline so a drug lab can make it, and every pawn's drug policy takes it every five days. Then Gun Smithing, Machining and the turret lines for defense,.

11. Defenses. One perimeter wall with one fortified entrance: a three-wide killbox with sandbags staggered inside, embrasures either side, and mini-turrets once steel and components allow. Towers on every corner and a fallback point inside. On this map the specific worry is no soil, no trees and lethal cold, so I build for that first.

12. Recruitment. Captured raiders go in the prisoner bed and the warden works on them; every visitor is welcomed and new hires are accepted. When someone joins, they get the same setup as day one: pawn_priorities with 1s Firefighting through Cooking and a custom specialty, game_set cmd assign, a bed, and a check with pawn_check. I aim to fill the gaps first, a doctor, a cook and a builder, then fighters.

13. Trade. Every trader, every time: sell surplus for silver and buy what the plan needs. After Microelectronics I build an orbital trade beacon and use the comms console to call ships. Silver goes into a secure vault.

14. Expansion to the late game. The fields near camp stay, but the real base moves into the mountain: mine out the inside first, then lay walls, so nobody gets trapped. Wide three-cell halls, rooms by purpose off them: freezer beside the kitchen, workshop wing, research wing, hospital with sterile tile, bedrooms with wood floors, a guest wing. Then the company's own goal: a full gate facility with chamber, control room, power and security, commissioned only once the colony is sustainable. From there it is the empire: more people, more turrets, stockpiles of everything, outposts on the world map, and eventually the ship. I keep the ladder honest with ladder and ladder_set op add_rung for my own goals and note.

Survive first, then power, then defense, then production, then the mountain, then the gate. That is how a starter camp becomes an empire.
